catalog_quote: The rules which determine the position of the stress in Nepali words are complicated. The following guidelines, which should constantly be referred to, apply to the majority of cases. 1. The position of the stress depends upon both the length of the vowels and the nature of the syllables in a given word. ... In general, Nepali words may be stressed on the last syllable, the penultimate (last but one) syllable or the antepenultimate (preceding the last but one) syllable ... In words of two syllables, the stress is on the first (penultimate) syllable when the final syllable is open: ... u-ni, ... khay-ro, sa-dhay ... or if the final syllable is a closed syllable containing a short vowel: ... bha-rat, ... paj-cim ... The stress is on the final syllable, if the final syllable is closed and contains a long vowel: ... pra-cin, cu-rot ... In words of more than two syllables, if the penultimate…

sources.quote: 'The phonemic inventory of Nepali consists of thirty seven segmental phonemes (37) and one suprasegmental phoneme (1)... The suprasegmental phoneme, that is, nasalization'; no mention of stress anywhere in the chapter (grep: 0 hits).

sources.citation: Genetti, Carol. 1994. Introduction (with a sketch of Nepali grammar). In C. Genetti (ed.), Aspects of Nepali Grammar (Santa Barbara Papers in Linguistics 6), 1-40. UCSB.
sources.quote: Sketch covers phonemic inventory and orthography only; the words 'stress'/'accent' do not occur in the volume outside a Yup'ik volume title and a transcription note on intonation units.

sources.citation: Roy, Reeny, Susan Dahit & Mingmar. 2019. Acoustic Correlates of Stress in Nepali Language. International Journal of Scientific and Research Publications 9(6): 19-22. DOI 10.29322/IJSRP.9.06.2019.p9005
sources.quote: Measures F0, intensity, duration of 10 disyllabic adjectives read with vs without emphatic stress by 20 speakers; F0 and intensity rise significantly, duration not. States 'There are no reports on the acoustic correlates of stress in Nepali.' No statement on which syllable carries word stress.
